doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Roadhouse gigs with Old Man Meyers and a rodeo
summary: Playing for seventy-five cents in Meyers's all-colored orchestra, and a bull loose at a rodeo.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And the list of people that you have, as you said, had patience with, is really quite impressive. And as a youth, you must have played some interesting gigs on the way up.
Strip shows? That kind of stuff? Whatever came along?

Hey man you know, speaking of that, we had this — there was a band. There was a man, a gentleman in L.A., his name was Meyers. And we used to call him Old Man Meyers. Jack and I used to play with him in his orchestra. He had I think three sons, one played piano, one played trumpet and one played I think bass if I remember. And he played trumpet. And Jack and I. And man, we used to play places where, roadhouses, where it was an all-colored orchestra, you know, which was a big deal, right? That type of thing. Anyway we’d play, well I’m just trying to think of places, incidentally we’d get paid, right? Seventy-five cents. I mean like half a dollar and a quarter. And we’d have a kitty. And we’d travel maybe 35, 40, 50 miles to these roadhouse places.

To make seventy-five cents plus the kitty, which would maybe come to a dollar, you know that type of thing. But anyway, playing, it was all part of it. It was all part of playing music, it was all part of being a musician, it was all part of, you know. One thing led to another, the experience you had over here helped you with the experience on the next gig, that type of thing. As a matter of fact what did you ask me? I forgot? What was the original question?
I was asking about just, you know, paying dues, and interesting kind of gigs that would come up.
Man listen, we played, I recall years ago man we played a rodeo.
Yeah. And we were on a flatbed truck, right? And man a bull, one of those charging bulls got loose and he jumped up on that. Terrible man. It was funny stuff.
Funny to talk about it now.
